issue.title: Fix WeakSequence circular reference
issue.body:
Fix WeakSequence circular reference

<!-- Provide a general summary of your proposed changes in the Title field above -->

### Description
WeakSequence's  `_remove` instance method had `__self__` which caused a
circular reference. Use a weak selfref to break the cycle.

Fix #5050 

### Checklist

body: you found this on code inspection?  The WeakSequence is only used in one little spot in the code and only involves teardown of mappers that use inheritance, not a standard situation nor one that is expected to be performant.    It is a bug though, thanks for the PR.

Hi Mike,

My application is taking up more memory than expected and that's why I'm looking into my application's gc output and find that SQLAlchemy is creating lots of garbage (circular-referenced objects) (10+ MB of garbage for one simple PK query) that cannot be cleared out with CPython's refcount and must rely on the gc module. I have identified and fixed a few places that creates circular referenced objects, mostly related to recursive calls of nested functions with closures, and this WeakSequence bug is the most obvious and easy one.

I am going to create another issue and PR for the other changes tomorrow because it involves lots of changes, and I would need your input on them regarding coding style / test methodology. These changes should make SQLAlchemy more friendly to CPython's refcount gc without hurting other interpreters / performance, but it may hurt code readability a bit. Please let me know if you do not want these kind of changes.

Hi Carson -

let's examine each change individually and determine their relevance.    Circular refs are IMO not always a bad thing and for those cases where objects are not expected to be torn down regularly like Table and mapper objects, they often provide a more performant navigation path than would be present if we put weakref.ref()s in between.  So a particular reference cycle needs to be addressed in terms of if the cycle is present in a structure that requires frequent, performant teardown, or if it is a permanent structure that benefits more from simpler navigational paths.

that said, invoking a query that is *not* also invoking configure_mappers() should not be producing any unreachable cycles.   Make sure you are calling configure_mappers() before calling this query.    Query cache improvements coming in 1.4 / 2.0 will also take pressure off of these issues as compiled objects will be cached more often.

**Carson Ip** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Fix WeakSequence circular reference** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1626

**Carson Ip** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **rel_1_3** branch:

**Fix WeakSequence circular reference** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1629

if we do find query-time cycles that are created I would want to prospose a new suite of tests within or alongside test/aaa_profiling/test_memusage.py, which runs some code and then asserts that no reference cycles, or an expected number of unreachable cycles, were created.

please review the tests proposed in https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/#/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1630 which hopefully should allow these cycles to be found and zeroing them out maintained.    So far, simple query scenarios do not seem to create cycles unless query.join() with certain kinds of arguments are used (which it shouldnt).

issue.body: test for Core and ORM operations with quickly disposed objects that nonetheless create reference cycles.    these should at least be tested and for very common objects like Query, loader option objects, etc. there should preferably few to zero cycles generated.

body: move on over to #5056 where a test suite is added and we can try to get some of these, mapperoptions not surprisingly seem to be a big issue but im not sure if those cycles can be eliminated without a lot more complexity.

update, all the cycles I've found I've managed to reduce to zero.  this is for query() using simple filter(), join() as well as query options.    you probably can find more cycles but the bunch that I've removed in the above gerrit should make a significant improvement in your test code.

Thanks for taking this seriously. This is moving real fast. Here's my personal playground and this eliminated most of the ref cycles I found in my application: https://github.com/carsonip/sqlalchemy/commits/optimization-clone
Most of the changes don't require weakref.
I am starting a new playground with a MCVE to verify that the changes resolve ref cycle. I'll let you know the progress.

Let me lay out what I have found so far, in categories:
1. Instances with PopulateDict attributes with instance methods as creator
    - `_class_resolver`
    - `ColumnAdapter`
    - `SQLCompiler` (fixed in master but not in rel_1_3)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9133397/71539575-42663e80-2979-11ea-80d2-b28cbed01a61.png)

2. Recursive calls of nested functions with closures (usually keeps a large number of garbage objects around)
   - clone methods under cloned_traverse, replacement_traverse etc
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9133397/71539587-66c21b00-2979-11ea-97b7-ff3bbc7fca50.png)

3. Instances with instance attributes pointing at self
   - what you pointed out in #5056 , including EntityRegistry, AliasedInsp
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/9133397/71539618-e51ebd00-2979-11ea-9262-d5abf90628e0.png)

Now that you are working full speed in gerrit, I'm not sure how I could help. Maybe I'll rebase my fixes on top of your patches and create a PR. If you have a better idea of how I could help, please let me know.

now..........is the issue you're having, that having lots of unreachable cycles is creating a larger memory footprint or the CPU time spent for cPython's GC to clean them up?      IIUC the gc collect runs at a particular interval so if the reference cycles are produced at a higher rate that will use more memory?    I am now getting into cycles that are necessary for performance, and removing them has a much bigger negative impact on call coiunts.
things seem to be a lot worse in 1.3 than in master for some reason which is strange

My busy application is exhibiting some kind of high water mark memory pattern, i.e. it is consuming more memory than it is actually using, e.g. tracemalloc / pympler showing dicts are using 300MB and strs are using 50MB but the application is consuming 1GB from OS's point of view.

My hypothesis:
The application runs query A, B, C sequentially and it keeps the garbage around. At this moment CPython already allocated memory to keep the garbage of A, B, C, instead of do A, clean up, do B, clean up...

that/s kind of strange, have you set the GC settings very differnetly or something?   note that interpreters like pypy do *alll* garbage collection asychronously so the cycles are usually brought up more as a CPU issue rather than a memory one.

I am using the defaults. The memory issue (and OOMs) may not be caused by SQLAlchemy because I also see ref cycle issues in another library I use, but I was thinking that avoiding ref cycle in CPython can't be a bad thing if it does not affect performance, and that's why I'm looking into this issue now. May not be as big as a problem as we may think, but I think it is a nice-to-have.

there's a 1.3 backport in https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/#/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/1631 which includes a backport of 1.4's newer "anon map" structure that no longer introduces a cycle.    you should confirm that the number of uncollected cycles is significantly lower in your test suite and assuming that's the case, see if it has an impact on OS level memory.  otherwise I'm inclined to go with what I have here and not much else.
